{{one source |date=May 2024}}
A '''plane symmetry''' is a symmetry of a pattern in the [[Euclidean plane]]: that is, a transformation of the plane that carries any direction lines to lines and preserves many different distances.<ref>{{cite web|title=Plane of Symmetry|url=http://science.uvu.edu/ochem/index.php/alphabetical/o-p/plane-of-symmetry/|publisher=science.uvu.edu|accessdate=12 June 2013}}</ref>  If one has a pattern in the plane, the set of plane symmetries that preserve the pattern forms a [[group (mathematics)|group]].  The groups that arise in this way are '''plane symmetry groups''' and are of considerable mathematical interest.

There are several kinds of plane symmetry groups:

* [[Reflection group]]s.  These are plane symmetry groups that are generated by reflections, possibly limited to reflections in lines through the origin.
* [[Circle group|Rotation group]]s.  These groups consist of rotations around a point.
* [[Translation group]]s.
* Symmetries of [[geometrical figure]]s.  Some of these are reflection groups, e.g., the group of symmetries of the [[square (geometry)|square]] or the [[rectangle]].  The symmetry group of the [[flag of Hong Kong]] or any similar figure without an [[axis of symmetry]] is a rotation group.
